finding: rules.md:101, branching-policy.md:41, and planning-agent.md:110 say that the prefixes next-id serves are listed in finding-format.md § File location and name. That list holds only the nine finding tags; ST, T, and ADR are missing, although next-id serves them (BR-068). Link BR-068 in validation-rules.md, or name all twelve prefixes in one place and link it.
why_this_severity: Each producer file names its own prefix (create-backlog: ST, todo-format: T, write-adr: ADR), so an agent still claims those IDs (no to fails_purpose); a reader who follows the link sees an incomplete list and must search for the rest (raises_cost).

finding: verify-story passes the abbreviated SHA to `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}`. Git resolves a ref name before an object prefix, so a branch or tag named like 4 to 40 hex characters (for example `cafe`) wins, and the ledger records that ref's tip as commit_sha. Pass `--disambiguate=<sha>` first, or check that the expanded SHA starts with the argument.
why_this_severity: The wrong commit lands in the ledger only when a hex-named ref exists, which the repository's naming does not produce (no to harms_downstream); the operator must then find and correct a recorded SHA (raises_cost).

finding: DEC-11, ADR-0031, architecture.dsl, arc42 5.11, and 6.15 give the counter port the operations claim and seed and put the retry and the wait in the git-ref adapter. In next-id, the protocol Counter has read and push, claim_loop in the script core runs the retry and the wait (next-id:347), and seed reaches git without the port (next-id:386). Move the loop and the seed behind a port with claim and seed, or have the architecture agent describe the port as built.
why_this_severity: Every behaviour of BR-071 to BR-073 holds and the tests drive claim_loop through the protocol (no to fails_purpose); a second backend, which ADR-0031 expects, must bring its own seed and fit a lease-shaped read and push instead of implementing claim and seed (raises_cost).

finding: Step 4 tells VIRGIL to set agent-factory.counterRemote to the parent of the directory that `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` prints. In the main worktree, that command prints the relative `.git`, so an agent may store `.`. BR-096 and ST-0379 require the absolute path. With `.`, a claim run from a subdirectory pushes to that subdirectory and fails. Name `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` and say that the setting holds an absolute path.
why_this_severity: From the project root and from a worktree, `.` still reaches the shared repository, and an agent that resolves the parent usually writes an absolute path (no to fails_purpose); a wrong value fails only in a subdirectory, so a reader must find the cause behind an unrelated git error (raises_cost).

finding: test_impl_0009_a_refused_push_finishes_when_origin_holds_c pushes exactly C to origin after the check. git then treats the move's push of C as up to date and accepts it, so the move finishes on the normal path and never reaches the branch `on_origin == move.sha` in `_after_refusal`. Make the push fail first, for example by wrapping `push_to_origin` to push C and then raise CalledProcessError, and assert that the branch ran.
why_this_severity: The branch is a few lines and the code reads correctly, and the resume collision of IMPL-0009 has a test that reaches `_after_refusal` (no to fails_purpose); a later change can break the finish-after-refusal branch with every test green (raises_cost).

finding: After DEC-16, a refused move keeps the marker, so every ID claim fails by BR-097 until a move succeeds. The claim message says that origin holds the counter, which is false when the push failed. The Collision and Another failure outcomes of the counter check tell VIRGIL to name the next session start as the next chance, but not that no story, finding, todo entry, or ADR can be numbered until then. Add one sentence to both outcomes: ID claims fail until the move succeeds, and VIRGIL can offer the move again in the same session once the cause is fixed.
why_this_severity: The move and the claims behave as BR-097 and BR-102 define, and no number goes out twice (no to fails_purpose); an agent that meets the failing claim must work out the cause from a message that names origin as the holder (raises_cost).
